schema.description: Schema version. Bump on any breaking change; a bump means a simultaneous redeploy of cloud, bridge and a rebuilt iOS app.

track_id.description: Stable across frames for the same physical object; unique only within a source. The consumer's refractory key is the pair (source, track_id), never track_id alone. A producer with no tracker (the phone) must still synthesize a key that is stable frame-to-frame for the same object -- e.g. cls plus a quantized bearing bucket -- because the refractory gate is the only anti-flooding mechanism.

t_capture_ms.description: Phone-clock Unix epoch milliseconds, D-corrected per camera-sync-design §4.3. Seconds or microseconds here are a bug, not a unit choice. The window deliberately rejects a seconds-valued timestamp (below the minimum) and a microsecond-valued one (above the maximum).

ttl_ms.description: Time-to-live in milliseconds, from the §4.4 staleness table. 15000 is the largest value in that table (scene description).

cls.description: Closed enum of 12 values. A detector class outside the 12 must be mapped by the producer, never emitted as a new string: bicycle -> cyclist, motorcycle -> scooter, truck -> car, anything else -> unknown_obstacle.

bearing_deg.description: Torso-relative bearing in degrees, 0 = ahead, + = right. Half-open interval (-180, 180]. atan2 returns exactly -180 for directly behind, so a producer converting radians to degrees can emit exactly -180.0 and be rejected; producers must normalize bearing_deg <= -180 by adding 360 before emitting.

range_m.description: Metres. Phone only, and only while §2.2 scale anchoring is healthy. Trustworthy to ~15 m (§4.5); the 50 m ceiling exists to catch a diverged scale factor, not to express policy.

range_band.description: near <= 5 m, mid 5-15 m, far > 15 m. Producers pick their own box-height thresholds to hit these; consumers may rely on these numbers. X4 always emits a band; the phone emits one when unanchored.

closing_mps.description: Line-of-sight range rate relative to the wearer, positive = closing (approaching), negative = receding. Not the object's ground speed: a cyclist at 6.7 m/s approaching a wearer walking 1.4 m/s toward them is closing_mps ~= 8.1.
